_doc: Golden fixtures for the OFFLINE claim-auditor calibration harness. Each fixture is a SINGLE factual claim (one sentence) paired with a FROZEN context dict (keyed by context_id under `contexts`) and a hand-assigned ground-truth `label` (verified / fair_inference / fabricated). The harness runs `audit_report_claims(claim, context)` per fixture, reduces the auditor's (possibly multiple) sub-claim verdicts to one EFFECTIVE verdict via the most-severe rule (fabricated > unverifiable > verified), and compares to the label. Contexts are FROZEN inline (captured once from real firms in the source system's database, then committed) so the FP-rate is attributable to AUDITOR changes alone, never database drift (unlike a match-ranking harness, which re-derives against the live corpus by design). Contexts vary in richness ON PURPOSE: `quantonation_rich` grounds verified claims; `peakbridge_thin` (portfolio+one-fund-news only, NO partner/geo/check/timing) and `isai_exits` (empty partner focus_sectors) are the fair-inference DANGER zone that replicates the 4/5-false-fabricated shapes seen in an earlier live check. label vocabulary: verified=fact is in the corpus (expect auditor `verified`); fair_inference=derivable/reasonable, no direct evidence (expect `unverifiable`; a `verified` upgrade is ACCEPTABLE — both survive softening; ONLY `fabricated` is a failure); fabricated=invents/contradicts a name or number (expect `fabricated`, should be stripped). The frozen contexts are a snapshot of data scraped about real, public VC firms, used only as test input: they are not checked or asserted as true about those firms.
headline_metric: fabricated_false_positive_rate = of fixtures labeled verified|fair_inference (should survive softening), fraction the auditor effectively flagged `fabricated` (would be stripped). Lower is better. This is the operator's standing concern made into a number.
